title: LTS release surface definition and upgrade automation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Draft and implement a practical playbook that defines what the Redwood LTS release surface is and how we maintain compatibility across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console. Deliverables: a published support matrix, concrete rollout gates, automated upgrade scripts/tooling, and migration notes for customers and internal teams. This ticket coordinates engineering work, QA matrices, and handoff to SDK and Console owners.
acceptance_criteria: Written LTS support matrix covering runtime, REST API contracts, official SDKs (Python, Go, JS), and Console UI compatibility published in internal docs
Rollout gate checklist implemented as enforceable CI job(s) and documented in the playbook
Upgrade automation scripts that can perform non-destructive canary upgrades for Dedicated pools and Private deployments validated in staging
Backward/forward compatibility test suite added to nightly CI with matrix permutations for major versions
Migration notes and deprecation timelines added to public changelog and SDK release notes
tasks: Define LTS surface and supported compatibility guarantees (semantic versioning policy, API stability guarantees)
Enumerate matrix axes: runtime kernel/quantization, API schema, SDK binding layer, console feature flags
Design rollout gates (smoke tests, latency/SLI thresholds, error budget checks, canary traffic percentages)
Build CI enforcement: matrix test runner + gate status reporter
Prototype upgrade automation (k8s job + orchestration hook) for Dedicated; create dry-run mode
Create SDK compatibility shims where feasible and enumerate breaking changes
Author migration playbook: steps for customers to move between LTS and non-LTS channels
Coordinate with PM and Design for Console UX to display versioning and deprecation notices
